lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: constant rate of change versus constant ratio
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: constant rate of change versus constant ratio

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A population of 1000 grows by 7% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 5 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 73 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
A stays ahead permanently because 73 is larger than 3.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 1800(0.97)^t, with t in years. What does 0.97 represent?
choices: the number of years until the asset is worthless
the total value lost over the asset's life
the value of the asset when it was new, $1800
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.97, meaning a 3% annual loss

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (6, -9) and (10, -17). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 9, 36, 144, 576. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 4.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 4.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: A population of 600 grows by 8% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 5 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 56 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: A stays ahead permanently because 56 is larger than 2.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
